I now have the full mechanism from primary sources: the complete `mcknap.c` implementation (partition/LP solver, dominance, core, fathoming), the EJOR 1995 abstract, codes.html descriptions, the book's chapter structure, the MCMKP techreport DP, and Chan's convolution machinery. Here is the extraction.

## Techniques from fetched sources

- **O(n) LP relaxation via gradient-median partitioning (no sorting)** | Pisinger, EJOR 1995 (abstract: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/037722179500015I) + implementation https://hjemmesider.diku.dk/~pisinger/mcknap.c; book §11.2.1 "Linear Time Algorithms for the LP-Relaxed Problem" (https://hjemmesider.diku.dk/~pisinger/knapsack/toc.pdf) | O(n) expected, O(n) space | Sample ≤15 random classes (`MEDIMAX=15`), take the **median gradient** (dp,dw) = (max-profit item − min-weight item) per class; project every option with **integer determinant** `DET(p,w,dp,dw)=p·dw−w·dp` — zero divisions/floating point (deterministic, exact); if capacity c lies between the classes' extreme weight sums, that direction is LP-optimal; else fix each class's extreme option, delete LP-dominated options (`separate`), repeat. Dantzig UB = `fixp + (c−fixw)·dp/dw`. Paper cites Dyer '84 and Zemel '84 O(n) LP algorithms as prior art. | **Pays off at small scale** — replaces sort+greedy; also yields the reported gap.

- **Within-group dominance = upper convex hull pruning** | mcknap.c `preprocess`/`domiitem`/`separate`; book §11.2 "Dominance and Upper Bounds" (toc.pdf URL above) | O(n) per pass | `preprocess`: per class find min-weight and max-profit items, delete any option with weight ≥ max-profit-item's weight but lower profit; fix singleton classes and subtract from capacity. `domiitem`: sort by weight, keep only strictly profit-increasing items (hull), park dominated at array end. During LP iterations: underfull ⇒ delete options with p ≤ LP-choice's p; overfull ⇒ delete options with w ≥ LP-choice's w. | **Small scale** — few options/group, so hull is nearly free and shrinks everything downstream.

- **Expanding core in gradient order, lazily partially sorted** | mcknap.c `defineedges`/`partsort`/`checkinterval`; https://hjemmesider.diku.dk/~pisinger/codes.html ("mcknap… first algorithm using the idea of a 'core'… median search… then dynamic programming… expanding core"); book §11.7 | O(core · log) work; classes outside core never enumerated | Each class contributes only its two **edge gradients** relative to the LP choice (best option above and below LP weight, found by determinant scan); two stacks sorted by decreasing/increasing gradient using lazy quicksort — unsorted intervals pushed on a stack and sorted only when the DP steps into them (`checkinterval`). Core grows one class per iteration from each side until fathomed. | **Small scale** — with tens of groups the core is often a handful of classes; LP UB frequently equals incumbent and DP never starts (codes.html: bounds "derived from the LP-relaxed solution, and if these do not coincide, dynamic programming is used").

- **DP on Pareto lists: merge-time dominance + gradient fathoming of states** | mcknap.c `multiply`/`merge`/`reduceset`/`findvect`; codes.html (minknap: "dynamic programming where enumerative bounds are used to fathom unpromising states"); book §11.5–11.6 | list length ≤ 2^core, kept tiny by pruning | `merge`: divide-and-conquer merge of a class's options into the partial-vector list, dropping any (p,w) that doesn't strictly improve profit at higher weight **during the merge** (sentinel max-weight entries replace bounds checks). `reduceset`: binary-search (`findvect`, switching to linear scan under `SYNC=5` entries) for the incumbent; then fathom every state with a two-sided bound — left states via `DET(p−z, w−c, pt, wt) ≥ 0`, right states via the opposite edge gradient. | **Small scale** — this is what makes exact enumeration microscopic.

- **Per-option reduction inside classes** | mcknap.c `reduceitem` | O(class size) | Before a class enters the DP, any option whose LP-completion bound (option + break gradient (pb,wb)) can't beat incumbent z is swapped to the end and cut (`DET(psum1−z, wsum1−c, pb, wb) ≥ 0`). | **Small scale** — direct option-count reduction in exactly our size regime.

- **Mixed-radix solution encoding (no parent pointers)** | mcknap.c `rotatesol`/`definesol` | O(core) traceback | Solution = one integer in mixed base (|class| per level); decode by repeated div/mod; `vtype vmax` guards overflow by dropping oldest digits. | **Small scale** — trivially portable to TS BigInt-free if core ≤ ~32 classes (matches `MAXLIST 32`).

- **Re-solve / warm-start evidence** | mcknap.c `definesol` + `used` flags; book §1.3 "Single-Capacity Versus All-Capacities Problem" (toc.pdf); MCMKP Algorithm 1 (https://msinnl.github.io/pdfs/MCMKP-techreport.pdf); Chan §2 (https://tmc.web.engr.illinois.edu/knapsack_sosa.pdf) | — | No fetched source describes perturbation warm-start for MCKP. Closest sourced facts: mcknap re-solves the same instance up to ~10 rounds with tightened z and c, skipping classes flagged `used` ("avoid recalculation"); the **value-function view** computes f(c) for **all** capacities in one sweep (MCMKP `M[k]`, Chan's f_I(x) step function) making capacity/profit perturbation re-solves a lookup rather than a re-run. | **Small scale** — ideal substrate for cross-turn hysteresis.

- **MCMKP DP details** | Furini/Ljubić/Sinnl (URL above) | O(nC) time, O(n+C) space | Exact-capacity DP (min profit occupying **exactly** k); critical item i_c bounds which options may be excluded (Prop. 1: excluded min-weight ≤ w_c); recovery via O(nC) bit-table + O(n) traceback **or** recursive re-solve keeping O(n+C) space (Props. 5–6). Computational result: DP beat CPLEX on 8/9 categories but collapsed on ~100× larger weights — evidence C ~ 10^4 is where naive DP arrays start to hurt. | **Small scale only** for the array version.

- **Chan's (min,+) machinery** | SOSA 2018 (URL above) | FPTAS O(n log 1/ε + (1/ε)^{5/2}); **small-n variant Õ((1/ε)n^{3/2})** (Cor. 12) | Round profits to powers of 1+ε (m distinct values); equal-profit items ⇒ greedy yields an exact **p-uniform pseudo-concave** step function (breakpoints = weight prefix sums); convolving uniform × pseudo-concave = Monge row-minima ⇒ **SMAWK in O(ℓ)** (Fact 1(ii)); round the other side to εb-multiples (Lemma 1); incremental vs divide-conquer merging of step functions (Lemma 2), combined (Thm 3). | **Mixed** — the ε-rounding + upper-envelope-of-step-functions trick is cheap and gives the ε-optimal escape hatch; asymptotic machinery is large-scale.

- **Sibling mechanisms (codes.html)**: expknap = B&B + simple LP bounds, adaptive core; combo = MTH valid inequalities surrogate-relaxed + minknap DP + greedy initial core; bouknap = gradual bounded→0-1 transformation inside expanding core; mulknap = lower bounds by splitting surrogate solution, subset-sum capacity tightening, reduction-based variable fixation; scknap = surrogate-relaxed cardinality constraint kills the strongly-correlated gap. (https://hjemmesider.diku.dk/~pisinger/codes.html)

## Shortlist — best effort-to-payoff for per-turn small MCKP

1. **Integer-determinant comparisons everywhere** (no float/divide) — determinism + speed for free (mcknap.c).
2. **O(n) median-partition LP relaxation** — microseconds at our size; supplies bound, gap, and break gradient (mcknap.c; EJOR '95).
3. **Within-group convex-hull + LP dominance preprocessing** — deletes options before any enumeration (mcknap.c; book §11.2).
4. **Pareto-list DP with merge-time pruning + two-sided gradient fathoming** — exactness with tiny state lists (mcknap.c; minknap lineage).
5. **All-capacity value function (M[k] / step-function f_I)** — one pass serves capacity perturbations and cross-turn warm starts (MCMKP Alg. 1; Chan §2).
